diagnostic_evidence.cuda_canonical_equals_cuda_independent_o: bit-exact, every canonical field: Llama 32 / 32 layers, Qwen 28 / 28 layers; synthetic Llama and Qwen geometries 60 / 60 full-state and 28 / 28 aging cases in both runs
diagnostic_evidence.cpu_canonical_differs_from_cuda_canonica: Llama 32 / 32 layers, Qwen 28 / 28 layers; the independent oracle differs across devices in the same way
diagnostic_evidence.mechanism_as_measured: floating-point device semantics diverge beginning at the scale calculation (max - min) / c: min and max are bit-identical on both devices; every CUDA scale value equals the CPU value of (max - min) * fp32(1 / c), while CPU computes true division. The one-ULP scale differences flip round() at quantization-code boundaries (codes differ by at most 1), and metadata codes and decoded values follow.

conclusion: cross-device bit-exactness is removed as a validity requirement. The quality run executes the canonical state on CUDA, and the canonical implementation equals the independent oracle on CUDA for both real models.
basis_of_the_amendment: independent same-device oracle conformance; NOT PPL / quality outcomes. No quality result existed before the amendment. The gate is not replaced by a tolerance, and the sizes above were not used to set any threshold.
separation_of_oracle_and_measurement: the frozen oracle (kvquant_k3.py) and its loader are NOT shipped into the PPL scoring container; canonical_rabit_quality.py remains the only RABIT implementation there; the oracle diagnostics are separate prerequisite evidence.
attempt_numbering: Attempt 1 remains permanently INVALID; any later PPL run is REGISTERED TWO-MODEL ATTEMPT 2, both models fresh under the amended protocol; Attempt-1 artifacts are never reused or pooled as quality evidence.
